items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sweet Pea was -- he was Duke’s alter ego really in a sense I’d say.

ctx.x: He’s going to get the verbatim transcription.

Duke Ellington was unbelievable man. As a matter of fact, he had a way with words that was really unbelievable man. If you wanted to say no, Duke made you say yes. If you wanted to say yes, Duke made you say no. Man, he had that extra sense of perception going, unbelievable. He was a master. He was something. Man I never will forget the first time that Duke, Lenny, Lena, and Sweet Pea, we were all in the same room and man you talk about a conversation. It was unbelievable. Just unbelievable man, and I’m sitting…

Their vocabularies were -- well Lena read a lot. She was an avid reader and Lenny was a very intelligent man. You know, to have all four of them in the same room at the same time was unbelievable. Tremendous experience. Tremendous experience.
